headline: Accepted consent agenda items and staff reports, tabled the by-laws until September, and sealed two non-public session minutes.
summary: Staff reported on fire department work, including a summer camp, facility roof projects, and equipment from Manchester Fire. The commission accepted the consent agenda items, the staff reports, and the EMS license investigation report. It tabled the by-laws until its September meeting and voted on how to handle three non-public session minutes.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda items 26 68 through 26 71.
Accepted and placed on file Chief Buxton's July commission report (Item 26 72 A).
Accepted and placed on file Assistant Chief Tremblay's July commission report (Item 26 72 B).
Accepted and placed on file Assistant Chief Pouliot's July commission report (Item 26 72 C).
Tabled the Board of Fire Commission By-Laws (Item 25 15) until the September 2nd meeting.
Accepted and placed on file the report on the EMS License Investigation (Item 26 65).
Accepted and placed on file, with regrets, the retirement notification from Private Michael Surette (Item 26 74).
Approved sealing the June 03, 2026 Non-Public Session #2 minutes, by roll call with 5 yea.
Accepted and did not seal the June 24, 2026 Non-Public Session #2 minutes (Item 26 77).
Approved sealing the June 24, 2026 Non-Public Session #1 minutes, by roll call with 5 yea.

REGULAR AGENDA 
 
Staff Reports: 
 
26 72 A Chief Buxton 
 
Chief Buxton expressed that he can address any questions regarding his submitted report and 
discussed the following: 
 Celebration of Life for Retired Deputy Telgen 
o Expressed thanks for BoFC support and members support during the services. 
o The members were there for each other and the Telgen family. 
o Thank you to NPD and DPW for their support during the procession 
 DPW discovered a sink hole at the corner of Lund/Almont and the procession 
was seamless, DPW took care of the sink hole and no DPW equipment was 
visible when the procession passed the area. NPD and DPW went above and 
beyond in this situation.  
o Thank you to Assistant Chief Tremblay and Assistant Chief Pouliot for all their help 
during the planning and event and keeping the department running.  
o Thank you to Local 789 President Cy Hebert for all of his work, countless hours, 
honor guard, etc. Cy is the honor guard commander. The organization is very lucky 
to have him.  
o Thank you to Deputy Armstrong and Deputy Mobley 
 EMS License Investigation is closed. The filings were unfounded. 
 
Commissioner Kelly noted that it was a profound display of support for Telgen family. 
Commissioner Kelly requested to pass along the BoFC’s thanks to Cy for all his work.  
Commissioner Melizzi-Golja said it showed him as a person not just firefighter. 
Commissioner Steere commented that Deputy Armstrong did a wonderful job as well as 
Retired Deputy Kirk, Deputy Mobley, and of course Retired Deputy Chief Telgen’s daughter did an 
exceptional job.  
Commissioner Burgess reiterated that all of the speakers did a wonderful job.  
 
Motion by Commissioner Kelly to accept Item 26 72 A, Chief Buxton’s July commission report, as 
presented and submitted, and place on file. 
Seconded by Commissioner Steere 
MOTION CARRIED 
 
26 72 B Assistant Chief Tremblay 
 
Assistant Chief Tremblay expressed that he can address any questions regarding his submitted 
report and discussed the following: 
 
 100MA100 Equipment from Manchester Fire  
o Master Box
Page 3 of 7 
 
o Manchester has discontinued the use of it and as they take their equipment apart 
they are giving it to NFR. 
o A lot of communities have not maintained their systems appropriately  
o Scraping like this works very well for NFR. 
 Training with Dispatchers 
o W1 would pick things related to time of year. 
o Tries to piggyback off of what the new hires on the floor are getting. 
 Training related to what’s going on out on the floor. 
 Train with the floor training 
 Assistant Chief Tremblay said that W1’s main focus is encouraging members to take the 
test and pass it. W1 is trying really hard to encourage study time and talking the positions 
up. 
 W1 has been given the authority to hire details to maintain the system because he doesn’t 
have a W2 right now and probably won’t until the fall. Details are filled by specialists first 
then it goes to the line.  
 W1 is juggling a lot of hats right now.  
 
Commissioner Kelly requested a monthly update regarding Fire Alarm.  
 
Commissioner Melizzi-Golja wanted to let everyone know if there is something that really needs to 
be talked about a Non-Public session can take place. 
 
Motion by Commissioner Lambert to accept Item 26 72 B Assistant Chief Tremblay’s July 
commission report, as presented and submitted, and place on file. 
Seconded by Commissioner Steere 
MOTION CARRIED  
 
26 72 C Assistant Chief Pouliot 
 
Assistant Chief Pouliot expressed that he can address any questions regarding his submitted 
report and discussed the following:  
 
 Facility Maintenance 
o Working to finalize roof projects and bring them to the Finance Committee  
o Waiting for paperwork from contractor to finalize a couple of things.  
o Station 2 roof will be next.  
o Replacing Building Controls at S4 – vendor is Viking Controls 
 Second Annual Nashua Fire Summer Camp is full and filled up quickly 
o Week of July 13th at Nashua Community College 
o Monday – Classroom, safety, overview of the week, handing out gear 
o Tuesday – EMS, CPR training, basic first aid 
o Wednesday, Thursday, Friday – the meat of the camp, will be outside doing practical 
training, they will have hands on training 
o Lt. Morin main instructor 
o 5 other members instructing 
o 8am – 3:30pm 
o Free Camp 
o Received donations for food, snacks, water
